RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination by itself — it's common in senior public-sector recruitment and is consistent with both fair and unfair outcomes. On its own it proves nothing, and leading with it can make a strong case look weak.

Your stronger ground is procedural: you were shortlisted, interviewed twice, and have waited two weeks with no written reasons. Chase that formally, in writing, with a deadline. Ask how the criteria were scored, how "experience of leading international projects" was weighted, and whether it appeared in the original advert — if it didn't, that's a real problem.

Mention panel composition only as context once you have the scores. Let the documents do the work.
